funds.name: AcE Fund (Fund of Funds - Accelerating Entrepreneurs)

size.raw: ₹299 crore committed to 88 biotech startups (as of April 2024)

strategy.thesis: BIRAC is the Department of Biotechnology's not-for-profit Public Sector Enterprise (Section 8 company, est. 2012) that is India's primary interface agency for de-risking and funding early-stage biotech/healthcare enterprises, deploying grants (BIG), product-development support (SBIRI, BIPP, PACE), and equity/fund-of-funds vehicles (SEED, LEAP, AcE, BIRAC-RDI) across therapeutics, diagnostics, medtech, vaccines and biologics.

lifesci.science_platform_notes: Runs ~100 Bio-NEST incubation centres nationwide and manages BIG, SBIRI, BIPP, PACE, E-YUVA, SEED, LEAP, AcE and BIRAC-RDI schemes on behalf of DBT.

track_record.portfolio_count: 15 lakh+ startups/entrepreneurs supported (cumulative, incl. non-equity grantees)

summary.en: BIRAC is the Government of India's (Dept. of Biotechnology) national interface agency and largest early-stage biotech funder, providing grants, product-development support and equity/fund-of-funds capital (AcE, SEED, LEAP, BIRAC-RDI) to therapeutics, diagnostics, medtech, vaccine and biologics startups.

name.en: National Biopharma Mission (Innovate in India / i3 Programme)

current_fund.raw: $250 million total (Govt of India + World Bank), World Bank contributing $125 million

strategy.thesis: A World Bank co-financed, DBT/BIRAC-implemented industry-academia mission ($250M total, launched 2017) to accelerate early discovery-to-development of vaccines, biosimilars, novel therapeutics, diagnostics and medical devices in India, building shared incubation, biomanufacturing and clinical-trial infrastructure alongside direct startup funding.

lifesci.science_platform_notes: Funded 100+ incubation centres, 25 specialised R&D/biomanufacturing facilities, 7 Regional Technology Transfer Offices, and clinical-trial capacity at 30 hospital + 10 field sites.

track_record.portfolio_count: part of ~10,000 bio-based research startups supported since 2014 across BIRAC's mission portfolio

summary.en: National Biopharma Mission is a $250M World Bank co-financed Indian government mission (implemented via BIRAC/DBT) that funds industry-academia biopharmaceutical product development — vaccines, biosimilars, diagnostics and devices — from discovery through early clinical stages.

sources.quote: The mission has catalyzed nearly 10,000 bio-based research startups since 2014 and supports development of vaccines, biosimilars, diagnostics, and cell therapies.

name.en: Centre for Cellular and Molecular Platforms (C-CAMP)

strategy.thesis: A Department of Biotechnology (DBT) initiative (est. 2009, part of the Bangalore Life Sciences Cluster) providing wet-lab bio-incubation space, an Investment Program for early-stage funding, and mentorship/acceleration to life-science startups in healthcare devices & diagnostics, drug discovery, biologics/vaccines and digital health, with focused programs on maternal & child health, AMR and COVID-19.

lifesci.science_platform_notes: Operates high-end lab/biocontainment infrastructure adjacent to NCBS-TIFR campus and a K-TECH TBI facility at GKVK campus.

summary.en: C-CAMP is a DBT-established (2009) life-sciences innovation hub in Bangalore combining bio-incubation lab space, an in-house Investment Program, and mentorship for healthcare devices, diagnostics, drug-discovery and digital-health startups; it has supported 350+ startups and recorded exits including Predible Health's acquisition by nference.

strategy.thesis: A statutory body (Technology Development Board Act, 1995; constituted 1996) under India's Dept. of Science & Technology that commercializes indigenous technology across all sectors via soft loans, equity and grants; runs biotech/healthcare-specific calls (e.g. 'CFP Medical Devices', 'Rare Disease Solutions Initiative') and has backed biotech-dedicated funds such as APIDC VCF (BioTech Fund).

summary.en: Technology Development Board is a Government of India statutory financing body (est. 1996) that provides loans, equity and grants for commercializing indigenous technology; it runs dedicated medtech/rare-disease funding calls and has invested in biotech-focused vehicles like the APIDC VCF BioTech Fund, though its overall mandate spans all technology sectors, not health exclusively.

strategy.thesis: Andhra Pradesh state-government-backed medical-device manufacturing and innovation zone that hosts AIC-AMTZ MediValley — India's largest medtech incubator, funded by NITI Aayog's Atal Innovation Mission and the Dept. of Pharmaceuticals' AMDTF scheme — plus a newly launched capital fund with MedArtha Capital to scale medtech startups and growth-stage device manufacturers.

track_record.portfolio_count: ~150 medtech startups supported to date; incubator capacity targeted to double to 300 ventures by 2026

summary.en: AMTZ is Andhra Pradesh's state government medical-device manufacturing zone and innovation hub, home to India's largest medtech incubator (AIC-AMTZ MediValley, backed by NITI Aayog's Atal Innovation Mission) and a newly announced capital fund with MedArtha Capital to scale Indian medtech startups.

strategy.thesis: A Government of Telangana venture fund (announced Jan 2026 at Davos as part of the state's Next-Gen Life Sciences Policy 2026-30) designed to catalyze early- and growth-stage investment in cell & gene therapy, precision fermentation, diagnostics, medical electronics and digital health, anchored around Hyderabad's Genome Valley cluster and intended to crowd in private/institutional capital.

summary.en: The Telangana Life Sciences Innovation Fund is a state-government fund of up to ₹1,000 crore (~USD 100M), unveiled January 2026 under Telangana's Next-Gen Life Sciences Policy, aimed at early- and growth-stage life-sciences and healthcare startups (cell & gene therapy, diagnostics, medtech, digital health) centered on the Genome Valley cluster.
